decisions_log.question: Java bare-vs-qualified method identity after the duplicate-traversal fix
decisions_log.decision: QUALIFIED ONLY. Java keeps `Outer.alpha` as type `method`; the bare `alpha` function element is DROPPED, not shimmed.
decisions_log.rationale: A nested-construct probe against HEAD showed the double-walk causes THREE defects from ONE root cause, not the one the ticket described: (i) exact duplicates, multiplicative with nesting depth - a C++ method at depth 2 emitted x4; (ii) MIS-SCOPED names - a nested type's members attributed to the OUTER type (`Outer.beta` for a method on `Inner`, `Outer.gamma` for a method on `Contract`), which are false facts rather than inflated counts; (iii) the bare/qualified fork. Because all three share the root cause they are not separable: any fix that removes the duplicates also removes the bare names, so preserving them would mean deliberately RE-EMITTING them as a shim - strictly more work than (A), built in phase 1 and deleted in phase 2 by this same program, since phase 2 (TKT-XGZA82) IS the bare-name reduction at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:63. Nothing in CODEREF-CORE itself consumes Java/C++/Rust elements (this repo is TypeScript), so exposure is downstream repos scanning those languages across a one-phase window.
rejected_alternatives: B - bare only: Java would stop producing methods and diverge from every other language.
C - keep both via a compatibility shim: considered and rejected as more work than A, with the shim scheduled for deletion in the very next phase.

decisions_log.summary: JsonVectorStore committed every mutation to memory before committing it to disk. Fixed with one snapshot/rollback wrapper across all three mutation paths.
decisions_log.scope_call: WIDENED beyond the ticket, deliberately. TKT-2ZSHSZ names upsert. delete() and clear() have the identical shape, and the mid-batch dimension check diverges the store with NO filesystem failure at all. Fixing upsert alone would have left two live instances of the same defect and a test suite that looked green.
decisions_log.design_note: Rollback over "mark the store unusable": the instance stays consistent AND usable, so a caller that handles the error can retry - pinned as its own test case. The snapshot is SHALLOW, and that is load-bearing: every mutation replaces a whole record entry or deletes a key, none reaches inside an existing record. Stated in the code so a future in-place edit does not silently escape the guard. Cost cannot dominate - save() already JSON.stringify-s the entire store on every mutation, so an O(n) key copy is strictly cheaper than the write it guards.
decisions_log.failure_injection: REAL, not mocked. vitest cannot spy on ESM fs exports; a mocked filesystem would prove only the test's own fiction. The tests create a DIRECTORY at the <storagePath>.tmp path save() writes to, so the real writeFileSync fails with a real EISDIR while the real store file keeps its real prior contents.

decisions_log.summary: GraphReRanker degenerate-input guards. The ticket framed this as non-finite scores; the measured damage is an ORDERING bug.
decisions_log.the_finding: rerank() ends with sort((a,b) => b.rerankedScore - a.rerankedScore). A NaN comparator result makes the sort implementation-defined, and MEASURED at HEAD a result the semantic layer scored 0 came back ranked ABOVE one it scored 0.5. One degenerate document silently reorders the whole answer. That is what the lead test asserts - ordering, not finiteness.
decisions_log.second_branch: The n/0 case never went non-finite and would survive an isFinite-only fix: Infinity capped to maxBoost gave boostFactor 2.0, so the result CLAIMED it had been doubled while its score never left zero. Pinned as its own case.
decisions_log.why_the_existing_guard_test_did_not_catc: graph-reranker.test.ts:159 is named "should handle zero weights" but zeroes only four of five, leaving semanticWeight at 0.2 - the sum is 0.2 and nothing degenerates. And its assertion toEqual(NaN, NaN) passes under vitest Object.is semantics, so a fully-NaN result set would have satisfied the very test meant to guard this.
decisions_log.design_call: Two degeneracies, two dispositions, deliberately. A non-positive weight sum THROWS - substituting equal weights would invent a ranking policy the caller never asked for, invisibly. A zero result.score CLAMPS to no-boost/zero - that is legitimate data from the search layer, not a configuration error. Also catches more than the ticket: weights that merely SUM to zero (+1, -1) were equally broken.
decisions_log.no_caller_regression: The pre-existing graph-reranker.test.ts passes 17/17 UNCHANGED alongside the throw.

decisions_log.summary: Two diagnostics reporting numbers nobody could act on. Both worse than the ticket states.
decisions_log.finding_1: QueryEngine.complex() did not time late - it timed NOTHING. `const start = Date.now()` was on the line immediately before `Date.now() - start`, after all filtering. The two calls were adjacent, so the method structurally reported ~0 regardless of work done. MEASURED: 31ms of real filtering over 20,000 records, reported as 0.
decisions_log.what_localised_it: Every other public query on the class is timed correctly, because they route through the private executeQuery() which takes `start` BEFORE calling queryFn. complex() is the only public query that bypasses it. The correct pattern was already three methods away in the same file.
decisions_log.finding_2: analyzeAnswer().processingEfficiency was a bare division: 100/0 -> Infinity, 0/0 -> NaN, on a field typed `number`. The consequence the ticket omits is serialization - JSON.stringify turns BOTH into `null`, so an MCP response or report file carries null where a number was promised and nothing raises. Asserted as its own case rather than settling for a finiteness check.
decisions_log.beyond_the_ticket: Added a negative-elapsed-time case: a clock adjustment mid-request would have reported a NEGATIVE efficiency. Finite, so an isFinite-only guard would have passed it through.
decisions_log.why_the_existing_test_did_not_catch_it: indexer.test.ts:559 exercises complex() but asserts only count >= 0 - true of every possible result - and never reads execution_time_ms. Same shape as phase 5 and phase 6: a test that exists, runs, and proves nothing.
decisions_log.disposition: Clamp, not throw - consistent with ADJ-17. A zero processing time is legitimate data, not a caller error. Denominator floors at 1ms rather than returning 0, so the metric stays a true lower bound and monotonic in token count.
decisions_log.no_caller_regression: pre-existing indexer.test.ts passes UNCHANGED alongside the fix.
